_comment: Per-phase model routing. Mirrors the skill's own phase table - Recon, Evidence, Synthesis, Verify, Report - plus the approved fix pass. The evidence workers fan out across axes A-H against a verbatim brief; synthesis and verification are where a wrong answer is expensive. See model-registry/references/routing-schema.md.

phases.why: Chooses Full or Delta and establishes stack, scope, baseline and artefacts. The load-bearing decision is whether a Delta baseline is present, unambiguous, verified and an ancestor - because the documented failure is a relabelled partial audit presented as a full one, which understates risk while looking complete.

adjust.why: An unverified or non-ancestor baseline forces the Full-or-stop judgement, which is the one call that decides whether the whole audit is honest.

phases.why: Each worker takes one axis with axis-brief.md verbatim and its documented run context. Bounded input, a fixed brief, and no cross-axis reasoning - the worker reads assertions and anchors every claim to file:line.

adjust.why: A wide axis fan-out means each worker's slice is one axis against a fully specified brief, which is the shape a cheaper tier handles without losing the anchor discipline.
Re-auditing against an open Critical/High backlog means judging whether a claimed fix holds, which is harder than reading the code for the first time.

phases.why: Maps behaviours to effective tests across every axis at once and routes findings into behaviour, suite-hygiene, measurement and n-a. This is the pass the per-axis workers cannot do, and its characteristic error is false confidence - declaring a behaviour covered because a test names it.

Independently refutes every Critical/High gap and every claimed resolution or downgrade. It is an adversarial pass against the audit's own conclusions, so sharing a tier with synthesis is the point; unusable verification retries once and then stands explicitly unverified rather than quietly passing.

Renders decided findings into the seven-section contract and stops. The judgements were made in synthesis and verification; this is faithful transcription that states mode, audited HEAD and any Delta range.

One approved slice at a time in a review worktree, demonstrating the new test can fail before it passes. The slice is already scoped and approved, but writing a test that genuinely fails for the right reason is not transcription.
